title: Pedestrian Crossing Controller
statement: Design a pedestrian crossing controller that waits in a default vehicle-green state and responds to a walk request. When the request is asserted, the controller must transition through vehicle-yellow then vehicle-red before asserting walk. The walk output should be active for one cycle and the controller should then return to vehicle-green after a short delay.
module_signature: module pedestrian_crossing_controller(input clk, input rst, input walk_request, output reg vehicle_green, output reg vehicle_yellow, output reg vehicle_red, output reg walk);
behavior: Normal operation remains in vehicle_green until walk_request arrives.
The controller transitions through yellow and red before asserting walk.
walk is asserted only during the dedicated pedestrian phase.
All state updates occur on the rising edge of clk.
rst is active-high and synchronous unless the problem statement explicitly says otherwise.
Use non-blocking assignments in clocked always blocks.
Outputs must never depend on uninitialized x/z state after reset.
When rst is asserted on a rising edge, registered outputs reset to their documented initial values.
constraints: Do not use combinational loops or latches.
example:
state | vehicle_green vehicle_yellow vehicle_red walk
Idle  | 1 0 0 0
Walk  | 0 0 1 1
hint: Model the sequence with named states and a state register.
